title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for hypertension.

Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 74, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 98% on room air, BMI 28.4.

Recent Labs:
Date: 10/12/2025
Glucose: 104 mg/dL
HbA1c: 5.7%
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2
Sodium: 139 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 20mg daily
- Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily
- Tiotropium 18mcg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily

Social History: 
Patient is a 51-year-old male who works as an office manager. He reports a non-smoking status and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. He lives with his wife and two children.

Family History: 
Father had a myocardial infarction at age 62. Mother has hypertension and type 2 diabetes.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, weight change.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain, palpitations, or edema.
Respiratory: Negative for cough, wheezing, or shortness of breath.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for abdominal pain, nausea, or diarrhea.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness or numbness.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain or swelling.

HPI:
[Copied Forward]
Patient is a 51-year-old male presenting for management of hypertension. He reports that his blood pressure has been stable at home, averaging 130/80. He denies any associated headaches or visual changes. He is adherent to his current regimen.

[Update]
The patient returns today for a follow-up. He reports that his blood pressure has remained well-controlled over the last month. He denies any side effects from his current medications. He expresses a desire to maintain his current routine.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, S1 and S2 heard, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Hypertension: Stable and well-controlled on current medication list.

Plan:
1. Continue current antihypertensive medications as prescribed.
2. Patient to continue home blood pressure monitoring and keep a log for the next three months.
3. Return to clinic in 4 months for a routine follow-up and lab work.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: An inhaler on the medication list does not establish COPD; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
